chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Husayn ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The drinker of wine will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with his face blackened and his tongue drooping, his saliva dripping upon his chest. And it is a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to give him drink from the essence of Khabal, or he said: from a well of Khabal. I said: 'And what is the well of Khabal?' He said: 'A well in which the pus of the adulterers flows.'

key_terms.طِينَةِ خَبَالٍ: The essence/mud of Khabal (a fluid in Hell)

ai.seo_question: What is the physical punishment and drink for wine drinkers on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni narrates this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to detail the specific physical torment awaiting wine drinkers, emphasizing the divine justice of quenching their thirst with 'Khabal,' identified as the pus of adulterers. This description highlights the interconnectedness of major sins in Shia eschatology, where the punishment for intoxication is linked to the bodily fluids of those guilty of illicit sexual relations, illustrating a precise retributive justice (Muqabala).
